title: Screening self-peptides for recognition by mouse alloreactive CD8+ Tcells using direct ex vivo multimer staining
protocol: Autoclave surgical instruments at the beginning of each daily session of surgery.
Weigh donor mice pre-operatively and record their weights.
Induce anaesthesia by using isoflurane at 3% and supplemental oxygen at 0.6 L/min.
Check the tail pinch reflex to ensure sufficient depth of anaesthesia before an incision is made.
Amputate the donor tail using a scalpel.
Euthanise the donor mouse by isoflurane overdose with cervical dislocation under anaesthesia.
Weigh recipient mice pre-operatively and record their weights.
Make a cranial to caudal inferior midline incision in the amputated tail of the donor mouse.
Mobilise the tail skin and remove it from the musculoskeletal structures.
Irrigate the tail skin with sterile normal saline containing ampicillin (10 mg/mL).
Flatten the tail skin and cut it into squares measuring approximately 10 mm × 10 mm.
Store the prepared grafts in sterile saline/ampicillin soaked gauze over ice.
Induce anesthesia with isoflurane at 3% and supplemental oxygen at 0.6 L/min.
Place the recipient mouse on a heat pad separated by 2 layers of sterile gauze.
Inject the recipient mouse subcutaneously with buprenorphine (0.05 mg/kg, 50 μL) for analgesia.
Inject prophylactic ampicillin (100 mcg/kg, 100 μL).
Inject 1 mL of preheated (41°C) sterile normal saline divided between 2 locations.
Apply a lubricating eye ointment to both eyes.
Insert a lubricated rectal probe for temperature monitoring.
Move the recipient mouse to the ventral position.
Prepare the dorsal skin with chlorhexidine 0.5% in 70% alcohol solution.
Shave the back and lateral thoracic regions from the cervical to the distal thoracic levels.
Check the tail pinch reflex to ensure sufficient depth of anesthesia before making an incision.
Reduce the inhalational anaesthetic concentration to ∼1% for maintenance after the incision.
Confirm adequate depth of anesthesia by testing the tail pinch reflex.
Prepare a graft bed on the back by sharp dissection and removal of skin approximately 10 mm × 10 mm.
Irrigate the graft bed with sterile normal saline.
Place the graft in the bed.
Secure the edges of the graft with small amounts of clinical grade cyanoacrylate tissue adhesive.
Remove the rectal probe.
Place a non-adhesive absorptive dressing on top of the graft.
Secure the dressing firmly with an adhesive cloth bandage.
Cease inhalational anesthesia.
Transfer the recipient mouse to the recovery cage.
Allow the recipient mouse to recover individually in an empty cage.
Line the cage with a disposable towel preheated on a heat mat set to 38°C.
Place only half of the recovery cage on the heating mat.
Monitor the recipient mouse for a minimum of 15 minutes.
Once awake and exploring, return the recipient mouse to a holding cage.
Singly-house the recipient mice.
Monitor recipient mice twice for the first 5 days post-operatively, paying special attention to urethral plugging detection.
Assess posture, activity, gait, respiratory pattern, hydration, bodily condition, hair, surgical wound, other abnormal signs, and body weight in recipient mice.
Monitor recipient mice daily for the next 5 post-operative days.
Remove bandage on day 7 post-transplantation.
Monitor grafts for rejection; deem skin grafts rejected when less than 20% of the graft remains.
Note urethral plugs can obstruct the urethra and lead to urinary retention, potentially causing renal failure if untreated.
Make single-dose aliquots from stock solution in sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes for vector preparation.
Store single-dose aliquots at -80°C.
Administer a single dose of 5 × 10^11 vgc per mouse via intravenous administration.
Thaw an aliquot on ice.
Add 500 μL of sterile PBS into the microcentrifuge tube.
Keep the diluted dose on ice.
Draw the diluted dose just before injection.
Induce anaesthesia with isoflurane at 3% and supplemental oxygen at 0.6 L/min.
Express the penis (for male mice).
Stabilize the skin overlying the penile vein using chlorhexidine 0.5% in 70% ethanol (for male mice).
Administer the AAV vector slowly intravenously via the penile vein using a 30G needle (for male mice).
Retract the penis back into the abdomen (for male mice).
Apply gentle pressure with a sterile cotton bud to achieve haemostasis (for male mice).
Warm the mouse using a heat lamp for 2–3 min (for female mice).
Prepare the skin overlying the tail vein using chlorhexidine 0.5% in 70% ethanol (for female mice).
Administer the AAV vector slowly intravenously via the tail vein using a 30G needle (for female mice).
Apply gentle pressure with a sterile cotton bud to the tail vein injection site to achieve haemostasis (for female mice).
Immediately post-operatively, allow mice to recover individually in an empty cage lined with a disposable towel preheated on a heat mat set to 38°C.
Dissolve lyophilized peptides (∼24 mg) individually in 500 μL of sterile DMSO.
Dilute the dissolved peptides in sterile H2O to achieve a final concentration of 5 mM.
Store the diluted solution at -80°C.
Pipette 50 μL of MBL QuickSwitch tetramer into a microtube.
Add 1 μL of peptide.
Add 1 μL of Peptide Exchange Factor.
Mix gently after each addition.
Incubate the mixture at 20°C for 4 h protected from light.
Pipette 20 μL of diluted peptide (400 μM) into a microtube.
Add 20 μL Flex-T monomer to the microtube.
Illuminate the solution with long-wave 366 nm UV light for 30 min on ice.
Incubate the solution at 37°C in the dark for 30 min.
Transfer 30 μL of exchanged monomer into a new microtube.
Add 3.3 μL of PE Streptavidin (0.2 mg/mL) to the microtube.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 30 min protected from light.
Prepare a blocking solution by mixing 1.6 μL of 50 mM D-Biotin with 6 μL of 10% sodium azide in PBS.
Add 2.4 μL of blocking solution to the microtube containing exchanged monomer and PE Streptavidin.
Incubate tetramer at 4°C for at least 16 hours protected from light.
Transfer 6 μL of exchanged monomer into a microtube.
Add 10 μL of 160 nM Klickmer-PE to the microtube.
Incubate dextramer at 20°C for 30 minutes.
Store assembled dextramer at 4°C.
Handle DMSO with adequate personal protection.
Place the mouse in an induction chamber and induce anesthesia using isoflurane at 3% and supplemental oxygen at 0.6 L/min.
Perform midline laparotomy to expose the inferior vena cava by gently moving intraperitoneal contents to the right.
Introduce a 22G cannula distally to the renal bifurcation.
Transect the hepatic portal vein to allow outflow of perfusate.
Slowly perfuse the liver with 20 mL of PBS at 20°C by manual injection over 1 minute.
Transect the liver lobes and transfer them to a 100 μm cell strainer.
Gently press through and wash with cold RPMI + 5% FCS (RPMI/FCS5).
Transfer the liver slurry into a 50 mL conical tube.
Wash the liver slurry twice with 50 mL RPMI/FCS5 by centrifugation at 400 × g for 10 minutes.
Decant the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 15 mL PBS.
Add 9 mL of Isotonic Percoll PLUS and mix.
Centrifuge the solution at 500 × g for 15 minutes, with no brake.
Discard the supernatant (containing hepatocyte debris).
Wash the liver leukocytes in the pellet once by centrifugation at 400 × g for 10 minutes.
Resuspend the liver leukocytes in 2 mL of red cell lysis solution.
Incubate for 2 minutes at 20°C.
Following this, wash the liver leukocytes twice by centrifugation at 400 × g for 10 minutes with RPMI/FCS5.
Dissolve dasatinib in sterile DMSO to a concentration of 10 mM.
Store aliquots at -80°C for no longer than 3 months.
Thaw a dasatinib aliquot at 20°C on the day of tetramer staining.
Dilute 10 μL of the 10 mM dasatinib solution in 2 mL of PBS to achieve a concentration of 50 nM.
Dilute 10 μL of the 50,000 nM dasatinib solution in 2 mL of PBS to achieve a concentration of 250 nM.
Prepare fluorophore conjugated antibodies in cold staining buffer (2% FCS in PBS) on the day of tetramer staining.
Ensure CD8 antibody is from the clone KT-15.
Wash cells once with staining buffer by centrifugation at 400 × g for 10 min.
Resuspend 1 million cells in 40 μL of staining buffer.
Incubate cells with 50 nM dasatinib for 30 min at 20°C by adding 10 μL of 250 nM dasatinib.
Spin pMHC tetramer at 16,000 × g for 1 min to remove aggregates.
Add 0.5 μg of pMHC-PE tetramer to the cells and incubate for 30 min at 20°C.
Wash cells twice with staining buffer by centrifugation at 400 × g for 10 min.
Incubate cells with mouse TruStain FcX (BioLegend) (1 μL in 50 μL of staining buffer) for 10 min at 4°C.
Add 0.5 μg of purified monoclonal anti-PE (PE001, 1 μL in 50 μL of staining buffer) to the cells and incubate for 30 min on ice.
Wash cells twice with staining buffer by centrifugation at 400 × g for 10 min.
Add surface antibodies (total volume of 100 μL in staining buffer per sample) to the cells and incubate for 30 min on ice.
Wash cells twice with PBS by centrifugation at 400 × g for 10 min.
Add viability dye ZNIR (total volume of 100 μL in PBS per sample) and incubate on ice for 15 min.
Wash the cells twice with staining buffer by centrifugation at 400 × g for 10 min.
Resuspend the cells in 150 μL of staining buffer.
Filter the resuspended cells through a 50 μm nylon mesh.
Cells are ready to be analyzed using flow cytometry.
